Empires & Puzzles Frosty Review: 3-Star Hero Strategy & Guide

Frosty isn't just a snowman; he was a revolution. As one of the first reliable 3-star Blue healers, he changed the landscape of rare tournaments forever. But with years of power creep piling up like snowdrifts, does this jolly summoner still have what it takes to freeze the competition, or has he melted away? We dive into the stats, minions, and strategies to find out.
Frosty: The Snowman Who Brought Heals to the Blue 3-Star Arena
Frosty, The Northern Sentinel: Cold Hands, Warm Heals

family. When he rolled into the game in December 2020, he was nothing short of a revelation. Before Frosty, the 3-star Blue roster was desperate for a dedicated healer, often relying on off-color supports or simply burning items to stay alive. Frosty filled that void with a festive grin, bringing not just healing but also minions to the party. He is a "Classic" event hero—simple, effective, and built with a clear purpose: keeping your pint-sized team alive.

Frosty’s design is a delightful mix of festive cheer and "don't mess with me" attitude. He’s a classic snowman brought to life, but instead of a corncob pipe, he’s packing a serious expression and some wooden armor plating. The "cool guy" pose with the folded arms (branches?) and the tipped hat gives him a surprising amount of personality for a ball of frozen water. He looks like the kind of bouncer you'd find outside a club at the North Pole—he's jolly, but he's here to do a job.

If you pull Frosty, level him immediately. He will likely be your primary healer for Rare quests, Challenge Events, and 3-star Tournaments for a very long time. He makes completing the "Rare" tier of events much safer and less item-dependent.

Frosty is the grumpy snowman with a heart of gold (and health). While he may have lost a step or two in the speed department compared to the new lightning-fast 3-stars, his utility remains undiminished. In the niche world of Bloody Battle tournaments, he is royalty. He doesn't just heal; he builds an army.
If you have him, cherish him. If you don't, check your stockings this winter.
